title: What Is That in Your Hand?
paragraphs:
What Is That in Your Hand?
The Day God Stopped Asking Moses About His Future and Started Asking About What He Already Had
There are moments when life feels like one long apology.
An apology for not being enough.
Some people spend years waiting for God to give them something new before they obey Him.
Yet one of the most powerful questions in all of Scripture was not about what Moses lacked.
It was about what he already possessed.
In Exodus 4:2, the LORD asked Moses:
At first glance, the question seems almost unnecessary.
The kind of thing nobody would notice.
The kind of thing nobody would post about.
The kind of thing nobody would celebrate.
The kind of thing people step over without thinking.
Yet God saw something Moses could not see.
Because Heaven has always specialized in transforming ordinary things into instruments of extraordinary grace.
The story begins long before the burning bush.
He probably imagined a future filled with significance.
A shepherd wandering through wilderness nobody wanted.
For forty years his life looked like a story that had already ended.
Many readers know what that feels like.
But the feeling of living with chapters you wish nobody knew.
The years wasted running from God.
The thing that still makes your stomach tighten when you remember it.
Yet Scripture repeatedly reveals a truth that the enemy desperately wants believers to forget:
God is not intimidated by broken histories.
In fact, many of His greatest stories begin there.
When Moses stood before the burning bush, he was not confident.
Again and again he argued with God.
What if they don't believe me?
What if I'm the wrong person?
Perhaps his most dangerous mistake was believing his limitations were greater than God's ability.
Yet secretly they believe their weaknesses are stronger than God's purpose.
Yet God instructed Moses to throw it down.
The moment it hit the ground, it became a serpent.
Then God commanded him to pick it up again.
The staff was transformed into a sign of divine authority.
The object itself was not the miracle.
The power was never in the stick.
The power was always in the One holding the universe together.
Many believers are asking God for new tools while ignoring what He has already placed in their hands.
Some have wisdom earned through suffering.
Some have scars that could become somebody else's survival guide.
The enemy loves convincing people that what they possess is insignificant.
God often begins with what already exists.
A widow had a jar of oil.
A boy had five loaves and two fish.
Yet insufficiency in surrendered hands becomes abundance in God's kingdom.
Jesus demonstrated this more beautifully than anyone.
When the Son of God entered history, He did not arrive through political power or military conquest.

"For when I am weak, then am I strong."
(2 Corinthians 12:10)

ὅταν γὰρ ἀσθενῶ, τότε δυνατός εἰμι
(hotan gar asthenō, tote dynatos eimi)
"When I am weak, then I am powerful."
Not because weakness itself contains power.
But because weakness becomes the stage upon which Christ displays His power.
This is the heartbeat of the Gospel.
Yet what appeared to be the end became the beginning of redemption for the world.
The prophet Isaiah foretold this centuries earlier:
Jesus took humanity's deepest scandal upon Himself.
The empty tomb became Heaven's declaration that failure does not get the final word.
That is why the story of Moses resonates so deeply.
Because it is not merely about a staff.
It is about every believer who has ever looked at their life and thought:
Because He wants to reveal what He can do through surrender.
Your past may still haunt you.
But throughout Scripture, God repeatedly chooses what the world overlooks.
The lesson is not that your abilities are amazing.
The lesson is that Christ is.
Maybe the thing in your hand is a burden.
Maybe it is a Bible gathering dust on a shelf.
Maybe it is a simple willingness to obey.
Whatever it is, surrendered things become sacred things when placed before God.
And perhaps that is why this story continues speaking across generations.
Because every believer eventually reaches a moment when God asks the same question.
But when Jesus is involved, small things have a history of changing the world.
If this article challenged you, don't keep it to yourself.
What is currently in your hand that God may be asking you to surrender to Him?
Because one surrendered thing in the hands of God can become the beginning of a story you never imagined.
And maybe the miracle you've been waiting for is already resting in your hand.
